parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented universal-exposure rule (facilities, custody, border screening all undocumented rather than hostile), and functioning courts that struck down criminalisation with appellate confirmation. The immigration bar names 'homosexual', not gender identity, and regional treaty obligations plus the state's own interpretation limit it. Social record: documented religious hostility, but dated (2011–13) and LGB-framed; highest regional acceptance polling; Pride since 2017; 2024 harassment act names gender identity. Offsets: government appealed the equality ruling, pledges lack compliance reporting, prison placement, port-of-entry enforcement and document-mismatch practice are unknown — thin trans-specific data. Silence is not safety, but the structural signals (decriminalisation, working judiciary, reform pledges, above-regional acceptance) point to reduced rather than elevated risk.
